root_idea.summary: The root centers on binding, tightening, and making something firm and secure, extending to reliability, trust, bonds, and solemn commitments.
root_idea.development: From physical firmness and fastening, the root develops meanings of trusting someone as reliable and of securing an obligation through a bond, pledge, or confirmed covenant.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed as the normalized Form III perfect verb وَاثَقَ.
Displayed under the normalized Form IV perfect citation form أَوْثَقَ rather than the supplied imperfect occurrence.
Displayed as the normalized nominal citation form مَوْثِقٌ.
Displayed as the normalized nominal citation form مِيثَاقٌ.
Displayed as the nominal citation form وَثَاقٌ.
Displayed as the adjective وَثْقَىٰ, normalized with the supplied Quranic spelling.

senses.definition: To bind or obligate someone by a binding compact or covenant.
senses.usage_conditions: A Form III covenantal use; the Quranic occurrence describes being bound by a solemn obligation.
A causative fastening construction, including firm physical restraint.

senses.definition: A pledge, binding assurance, or formally secured undertaking.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic Yusuf passages, it is a pledge or promise given as security and guarantee.

senses.definition: A solemnly confirmed covenant, compact, or formally binding agreement or obligation.
senses.usage_conditions: A covenant confirmed by oath and عهد; the Quran uses it for divine-human commitments as well as binding agreements, treaties, and contracts.

senses.definition: A bond, fetter, or other means of binding.
senses.usage_conditions: A noun for what is used to bind; Quranic contexts present it as the bond or restraint imposed on a captive or offender.

senses.definition: The firmest, most secure, or most trustworthy.
senses.usage_conditions: The feminine superlative of أَوْثَق; in Quranic expressions it is substantivized for what provides the firmest or most reliable security.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become firm, stable, fast, or strong.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive Form I use describing the attainment of firmness or established strength.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To trust, rely on, or confide in someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Constructed with بِـ for the person or thing trusted.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make something firm, stable, fast, or strong.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative Form IV use distinct from the more specific use of binding or tying.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become firm or tight, especially of a knot.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form V intransitive construction describing a knot becoming secure.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To secure oneself against someone by taking or receiving a bond or guarantee.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction may describe obtaining a pledge or otherwise making oneself secure against a person or obligation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To close or secure a door firmly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form X construction applied to firmly securing a physical closure.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To confide in someone or place trust in him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form X construction with بِـ for the person trusted.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A trustworthy, reliable, or honest person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used as an epithet and also substantively; its plural is ثِقَاتٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Trust, confidence, or certainty placed in someone or something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs in expressions of having or lacking confidence or assurance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Firm execution of an affair and adoption of the sure method.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional expression for handling something securely and carefully.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bond, security, pledge, or written obligation for payment or performance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May denote a written security or document of obligation, as well as the pledge itself.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the surest or firmest manner.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A superlative expression describing the most secure method of proceeding in an affair.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One in whom, or something in which, trust or confidence is placed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive participial expression for a trusted or relied-upon person or thing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel firm, strong, or compact in build.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized descriptive expression for a she-camel of notably solid constitution.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Firm binding meaning represented under the Quranic Form IV.
Securing oneself by obtaining a bond represented.
Debt-writing for self-securing is covered by the bond or guarantee use.
Lack of confidence is covered by the confidence meaning.
Firm method and execution meaning represented.
Bond, security, and written obligation meaning represented.
Pledge is covered by the bond and security meaning.
Compact, covenant, bond, obligation, and promise branch represented under مَوْثِق.
Trusted or relied-upon person or thing represented.

cautions: مِيثَاقٌ and مَوْثِقٌ overlap in translations such as covenant, promise, and contract; the former is presented as a solemnly confirmed compact, while the latter is the pledged assurance or security exacted in the Yusuf passages.

English renderings such as ratification, treaty, contract, promise, and bond reflect contextual realizations of the lexical branches and are not treated as independent senses without corresponding lexical evidence.
